title: customer-upgrade-assisted-retirement-flow-and-notice-cadence
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Goal: Retire legacy v1 inference API surface while minimizing customer friction by providing automated compatibility adapters, a tiered notice cadence, and operational runbooks for support and success teams. This ticket coordinates launch planning, release notes, and go-to-market tasks across Product, Engineering, Docs, Support, Sales, and Legal.

Scope: 1) Automated compatibility adapter shipped in SDKs + server-side routing shim; 2) Multi-stage customer notice cadence (announcement, migration window reminders, final cutoff); 3) Console and API flags to allow opt-out / compatibility mode for high-risk customers; 4) Playbooks for support and account teams; 5) Release notes and developer migration guide with examples and migration scripts.

Non-goals: Building a permanent backward-compatibility layer -- adapter is temporary maintenance window with telemetry for deprecation metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility adapter implemented in Node and Python SDKs and feature-flagged on server routing
Developer migration guide live in docs with step-by-step examples and code snippets
Release notes prepared and signed off by Legal and Marketing 7 days before announcement
Console UI shows deprecation banner for affected routes and allows customers to request extended support
Support runbook published and 2 training sessions delivered to Support and Solutions Engineering
Telemetry dashboards track usage of deprecated endpoints and adapter switch-over rates
rollout_timeline: 2026-04-05: Beta of compatibility adapter in SDKs + internal dogfood on Redwood-hosted tenants
2026-04-20: Public announcement blog + email to active customers (90-day notice window begins)
2026-05-15: Release notes versioned and linked from Console; migration guide published
2026-06-01: Automatic routing shim enabled for customers who opt-in during migration window
2026-06-15: Deadline for extended-support requests (last day to apply for paid extension)
2026-06-30: Final cutoff: deprecated endpoints return 410 with migration instructions in response
2026-07-07: Post-cutoff review and incident retrospective; retention of deprecation metrics
cross_team_actions: Engineering: implement adapter pattern and server-side routing feature flag; provide migration telemetry hooks
Docs: draft migration guide, quickstart, API diff, code samples for Node/Python/Go
Support: draft runbook, escalations, and prepare FAQs; schedule training sessions
Marketing: coordinate announcement, segmented email lists, and blog post; prepare social copy and customer webinar
Sales: prepare playbook for enterprise customers including contract amendment template and paid-extension offers
Legal: review release notes and extension terms; sign off on public comms
Console: add persistent banner for affected accounts and a self-serve migration dashboard
comms_plan: Announcement + blog post + targeted email to owners of active deprecated endpoints (90 days before cutoff)
Weekly migration tips in product changelog and in-console messaging during 90-day window
Two webinars (Tech Deep Dive for engineers and Business Impact for executives) during the first 30 days
Reminder emails at 60, 30, and 7 days before cutoff; one final 24-hour notice for customers with opted-in extended support
Post-cutoff report shared internally and to impacted customers summarizing outcomes and next steps
risks: High-volume customers may rely on undocumented behaviors causing regressions when upgraded
Adapter does not perfectly replicate edge-case semantics leading to silent correctness issues
Announcement triggers surge in support tickets overwhelming Support capacity
Legal or contract obligations restrict automatic cutoff for some enterprise customers
mitigations: Pre-release compatibility testing and expanded dogfooding with selected large customers
Telemetry capture for mismatched responses and automated rollback for adapter when error thresholds exceeded
Staggered enablement with early access program for top accounts and an apply-for-extension workflow
Coordinate with Legal and Sales to generate custom cutoff schedules where contractually required
notes: Prefer opt-in adapter during migration window to reduce blast radius; enable auto-adapter only for low-risk traffic tiers.
We will run a short A/B study to measure adapter fidelity vs native calls before increasing auto-enable percentage.
Consider a lightweight CLI tool to assist large customers with batch migration of webhook endpoints and routing rules.
